opennyai_summary.final__facts:
His first application has been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 28.08.2024.
Appellant stood convicted u/S 354-A of IPC and sentenced to undergo 02 years sentence of rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,000/-; under Section 506 Part-1, of IPC sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 01 year with fine of Rs.1,000/-; under Section 450 of IPC, sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 05 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- and under Section 376 of IPC sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 10 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulation vide judgment of conviction and sentence dated 13.06.2024, passed by II nd Additional Sessions Judge, Mahidpur, District Ujjain(M.P.) in S.T. No.04/2022.
PS Jharda had registered FIR No.348/2021(Annexure-D/2) wherein it was alleged that the uncle of the prosecutrix had objected to relations of appellant with prosecutrix.
Thereafter, the appellant was assaulted on same dispute.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Learned counsel further contended that the prosecution in the present matter is a counter blast to that FIR.
It is a case of consensual relationship between the parties which is reflected from overall circumstances.
Per contra, learned Counsel for respondent State opposes the application and prays for its rejection.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
The learned trial Court ignored this important aspect of the matter.
The appellant was on bail during trial and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
He is undergoing sentence of imprisonment since the date of judgment i.e. 13.06.2024.
There is no likelihood of early hearing of appeal in near future.
It is,
accordingly directed that execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended during pendency of this appeal and he shall be enlarged on bail subject to furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial 3 CRA-7202-2024 Court for compliance with following conditions:-
(1). The appellant shall deposit the amount of fine (if not deposited) forthwith;
(2). The appellant shall appear before the Trial Court on 12th of March, 2025 and on such further dates as may be directed by the Trial Court;
(3). The appellant shall ensure hearing of the appeal on the date fixed for such hearing and shall also ensure proper legal representation on his behalf, on the date notified for hearing.
In case of breach of any of the aforementioned conditions, this order granting suspension of sentence shall become ineffective.
The Trial Court shall be authorized to grant exemption from attendance to the appellant on any date, on sufficient cause being shown [Chapter XIII Rule 42 Sub-Rule 2 of the M.P. High Court Rules, 2008].
Where the appellant does not appear on the date of his appearance before the Trial Court and no sufficient cause for non-appearance is shown, the Trial Court shall be authorized to issue non-bailable/bailable warrants to secure his attendance under intimation to the Registry of High Court.
The Trial Court shall also proceed under Section 446 of CrPC against such appellant and his surety without any reference to this Court and without any impediment of the order granting bail.
[Chapter XIII Rule 42 Sub-Rule 3 of M.P. High Court Rules, 2008].
4 CRA-7202-2024 On arrest/surrender in compliance with the warrant, the appellant shall be forwarded in custody to undergo sentence of imprisonment under intimation to the Registry of this Court.
Accordingly, IA No.19830/2024 stands allowed and disposed of.
List for final hearing in due course.
